app.title: WinCleaner
danger.title: Dangerous Action
danger.message: This change can affect system stability or security. Check the box and confirm to continue.
danger.anticheat.title: Anti-Cheat Risk Warning
danger.anticheat.message: This gaming tweak (VBS / HPET / MMCSS) can conflict with anti-cheat systems such as Riot Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC), or BattlEye. Possible outcomes include blue screens (BSOD), game crashes, or account bans. Only continue if you accept these risks.
common.adminRequired: This change requires Administrator privileges. Restart WinCleaner with "Run as administrator".
common.rebootRequired: Change saved. Restart your PC for it to take full effect.
common.comingSoon: Quick tips: 1) Turn on Game Mode before you launch a game. 2) Stop Xbox Game Bar from recording in the background (it can cost FPS). 3) In games, use Fullscreen / Exclusive fullscreen when you can. 4) Set your monitor refresh rate (Hz) to the highest value in Windows. 5) Keep your NVIDIA/AMD drivers updated. Manage V-Sync from each game’s own settings — it does not behave the same in every title.
dash.title: Dashboard
dash.subtitle: A snapshot of your PC and quick actions — you can start with one click from here
dash.quick.dnsDesc: Clear DNS cache for fresher lookups
svc.title: Services
svc.subtitle: Small programs Windows keeps running in the background. Turning off the ones you do not need lets your PC breathe easier. Toggle = Disabled.
tel.title: Telemetry & Privacy
tel.subtitle: Reduces what Windows tracks and reports to Microsoft. It will not magically boost game FPS; it is mainly for privacy and less background load.
blo.title: Bloatware
blo.subtitle: Preinstalled apps most people never open. Remove what you do not use, or reinstall via Store ID when available.
blo.critical: Required by system — removal disabled (so you cannot break Windows by accident)
blo.confirm: Selected apps will be permanently removed. WinCleaner cannot magically bring them back — you will need to reinstall from the Store. Continue?
blo.onedriveConfirm: Uninstall OneDrive completely? Cloud folder sync will stop. You will need to confirm twice.
gam.title: Gamer Optimizations
gam.subtitle: Settings for FPS, latency, and background noise. Do not expect miracles — a good PC plus these tweaks means cleaner performance.
vis.title: Visual Effects
vis.subtitle: The fancy window effects (animations, transparency). Turning them off makes the desktop simpler and lighter — especially noticeable on weaker PCs.
win11.title: Windows 11 & UI
win11.subtitle: Windows 11-specific UI and privacy tweaks: classic context menu, Copilot/Recall, Start recommendations, and Widgets.
net.title: Network Optimization
net.subtitle: DNS, NetBIOS, and bandwidth settings — for ping and name resolution in online games.
net.dns.title: Quick DNS Changer
net.dns.desc: Changes DNS servers on adapters that have IP enabled, then flushes the DNS cache. Needs Administrator.
tools.title: System Tools
tools.subtitle: Cleanup, repair, and maintenance. Risky items are marked red/yellow — read before you run them.
tools.sfcDism.confirm: This runs DISM RestoreHealth, then sfc /scannow. It can take a long time (10–60+ min) and may need internet. Continue?
tools.winsxs.confirm: StartComponentCleanup /ResetBase permanently removes superseded updates; rolling back older packages becomes harder. Confirm to continue.
tools.godMode.done:
God Mode folder created on the desktop:
{0}
tools.wuReset.confirm: wuauserv, bits, and cryptsvc will be stopped; SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 will be renamed; then services will restart. Administrator required. Continue?
tools.networkReset.confirm: Network settings will be reset to factory defaults; you should reboot afterward. Continue?
tools.networkReset.reboot: Network reset finished. Reboot the PC for changes to take effect.
tools.desc.restore: Create a Windows restore point before you change things.
tools.desc.cleanTemp: Deletes Windows and user temporary files.
tools.desc.diskCleanup: Opens the built-in Disk Cleanup tool.
tools.desc.sfcDism: Repairs system files — can take a long time.
tools.desc.winsxs: Cleans old Windows Update components — harder to roll back afterward.
tools.desc.godMode: Creates a desktop shortcut to every Control Panel item.
tools.desc.wuReset: Resets Windows Update services and caches.
tools.desc.networkReset: Resets the Winsock/IP stack — reboot afterward is recommended.
tools.desc.diskAnalyze: Shows free space across your drives.
tools.takeOwn.name: Context Menu: Take Ownership
tools.takeOwn.desc: Adds Take Ownership to file and folder right-click menus. Needs Administrator; turning it off removes the menu entries.
pre.title: Presets
pre.subtitle: Ready-made bundles: apply many settings at once with one click. You see a preview first, then confirm.
set.title: Settings
set.subtitle: Language, safety, and logs — manage how WinCleaner itself behaves from here
set.restore: Create a restore point when the app starts (recommended). Changes during the session do not create additional points.
restore.statusNone: No restore point was created for this session yet.
restore.statusOk: Restore point is ready for this session.
restore.failed: Could not create a restore point. System Restore may be turned off.
restore.warnBody: This can take about a minute. Please wait — WinCleaner will unlock when finished.
set.dangerous: Allow dangerous actions (only if you know what you are doing)
set.updates: Check for updates on startup (optional, requires internet)
set.updateAvailable: A new version is available: {0} (current: {1}). Open the download page?
set.updateCurrent: You are up to date — version {0}.
dlg.dangerBody: This change can break the system or weaken security. Check the box, then confirm. If you are not sure, click Cancel.
dlg.dangerCheck: I understand the risks and am doing this on purpose
dlg.blocked: This item is intentionally locked. Turning it off could break Windows; WinCleaner will not allow it.
svc.diagtrack.name: Connected User Experiences (DiagTrack)
svc.diagtrack.desc: Sends Windows usage data to Microsoft. Turning it off cuts background reporting — most people notice nothing. It won’t magically raise FPS, but you get better privacy and less background noise.
svc.dmwappush.name: Device Management WAP Push
svc.dmwappush.desc: Old-style push and device-management messaging, plus related telemetry. Most home users can turn it off and never notice.
svc.wer.name: Windows Error Reporting
svc.wer.desc: Sends crash reports to Microsoft when a program fails. It doesn’t prevent crashes — Manual is usually enough if you don’t care about those reports.
svc.xblauth.name: Xbox Live Auth Manager
svc.xblauth.desc: Handles sign-in for Xbox, Microsoft account games, and Game Pass. Only disable it if you never use Xbox or Game Pass — otherwise the Xbox app, some games, and friends list can break.
svc.xblgame.name: Xbox Live Game Save
svc.xblgame.desc: Syncs Xbox cloud saves. Local saves still work if you turn it off, but cloud sync may stop — be careful if you use Game Pass.
svc.xboxnet.name: Xbox Live Networking
svc.xboxnet.desc: Keeps Xbox online features connected. Turning it off can affect multiplayer and Xbox social features.
svc.xboxgip.name: Xbox Accessory Management
svc.xboxgip.desc: Manages Xbox controllers and accessories. Leave it alone if you use a wireless Xbox controller.
svc.spooler.name: Print Spooler
svc.spooler.desc: Sends print jobs to your printer. If you never print at home, turning it off frees a useless idle service — but printing and PDF print will stop working.
svc.bthserv.name: Bluetooth Support
svc.bthserv.desc: Powers Bluetooth headphones, mice, and controllers. Only turn it off if you never use Bluetooth — otherwise Bluetooth dies completely.
svc.onesync.name: Sync Host (OneSync)
svc.onesync.desc: Syncs Mail, Calendar, Contacts, and similar accounts. Built-in Mail/Calendar sync may break if you disable it.
svc.cdp.name: Connected Devices Platform
svc.cdp.desc: Runs Nearby sharing and phone–PC bridge features. Games are fine without it; those sharing features just stop.
svc.diagsvc.name: Diagnostic Execution Service
svc.diagsvc.desc: Runs Windows troubleshooters in the background. Manual means it only runs when needed, with less daily load.
svc.dusm.name: Data Usage
svc.dusm.desc: Feeds the data-usage counter in Settings. Turning it off may break the counter, not your internet.
svc.sysmain.name: SysMain (Superfetch)
svc.sysmain.desc: Tries to predict and preload apps into memory. On SSDs that can mean busy disk for little gain — many gamers turn it off to calm 100% disk spikes.
svc.wsearch.name: Windows Search
svc.wsearch.desc: Builds a search index in the background and keeps poking the disk. Start search gets slower without it, but search still works and the disk rests.
svc.rpcss.name: Remote Procedure Call (RPC)
svc.rpcss.desc: Windows’s internal communication layer — almost everything depends on it. Disabling it breaks the system. WinCleaner locks this on purpose.
svc.dcom.name: DCOM Server Process Launcher
svc.dcom.desc: Lets programs call each other at a low level. Turning it off wrecks Windows. Locked on purpose.
svc.windefend.name: Windows Defender Antivirus
svc.windefend.desc: Windows’s built-in antivirus. Don’t disable it here even if you install another antivirus — WinCleaner blocks that path on purpose.
svc.wuauserv.name: Windows Update
svc.wuauserv.desc: Downloads and installs security updates. Stopping it means quiet days now and growing security holes later — only if you know what you’re doing.
svc.bits.name: Background Intelligent Transfer
svc.bits.desc: Background downloads for Windows Update and some other apps. Turning it off can break updates and those downloads.
svc.pcasvc.name: Program Compatibility Assistant (PcaSvc)
svc.pcasvc.desc: Watches for program compatibility issues and reports them to Microsoft. Apps still run if you turn it off; the prompts may just stop.
svc.lfsvc.name: Geolocation Service (lfsvc)
svc.lfsvc.desc: Gives apps your location (pairs with the Deny Location tweak). Maps, weather, and other location features stop without it.
svc.remoteregistry.name: Remote Registry
svc.remoteregistry.desc: Lets other PCs on the network edit this machine’s registry remotely. Home users don’t need it — safer left off.
svc.ssdpsrv.name: SSDP Discovery
svc.ssdpsrv.desc: Automatically finds UPnP devices on your network (smart TVs, printers, and so on). Internet still works if you turn it off; discovery may need to be manual.
svc.upnphost.name: UPnP Device Host
svc.upnphost.desc: Hosts UPnP devices together with SSDP Discovery. Some network device sharing may stop if you disable it.
svc.retaildemo.name: Retail Demo
svc.retaildemo.desc: Store / demo-mode service for retail PCs. Useless at home — safe to disable.
svc.wmpnetwork.name: Windows Media Player Network Sharing
svc.wmpnetwork.desc: Shares Windows Media Player libraries over the home network (DLNA). Local playback is fine without it.
svc.tabletinput.name: Touch Keyboard and Handwriting
svc.tabletinput.desc: Touch keyboard, pen, and handwriting. On a desktop or laptop without a touchscreen you can usually turn it off safely.
app.3dviewer.name: 3D Viewer
app.3dviewer.desc: Views 3D model files. Most people never need it — safe to remove, and you can get it back from the Microsoft Store.
app.mixedreality.name: Mixed Reality Portal
app.mixedreality.desc: Setup portal for VR / mixed reality headsets. Without a headset it’s just wasted space — safe to remove.
app.xboxapp.name: Xbox Console Companion
app.xboxapp.desc: The older Xbox companion app. Think twice if you use Game Pass — some social and Game Pass features may depend on it.
app.xboxoverlay.name: Xbox Game Bar
app.xboxoverlay.desc: The Win+G Game Bar overlay — recording, widgets, FPS counter. Removing it cuts background capture load and can free a bit of FPS; reinstall from the Store if you miss it.
app.xboxidentity.name: Xbox Identity Provider
app.xboxidentity.desc: Identity provider for your Xbox account. Don’t remove it if you sign into Xbox services.
app.skype.name: Skype
app.skype.desc: Classic Skype video chat. If you already use Discord or Teams, you can usually remove it.
app.solitaire.name: Solitaire Collection
app.solitaire.desc: Microsoft’s card and casual games pack. If you don’t play it, it’s just sitting on disk — safe to remove.
app.weather.name: Weather
app.weather.desc: Bing Weather app/widget. If you check weather on your phone, you don’t need it on the PC.
app.news.name: News
app.news.desc: Bing News / headlines app. Remove it if you don’t want news shoved at you on the PC.
app.officehub.name: Office Hub
app.officehub.desc: A “try / buy Office” promo hub. You don’t need it whether you own Office or not.
app.people.name: People
app.people.desc: Contacts / address book app. Fine to remove if you don’t keep contacts there.
app.feedback.name: Feedback Hub
app.feedback.desc: Sends feedback and suggestions to Microsoft. Safe to remove if you never open it.
app.gethelp.name: Get Help
app.gethelp.desc: Microsoft’s help chat and tips app. Skip it if you just search the web when something breaks.
app.getstarted.name: Get Started
app.getstarted.desc: New-PC tips tour. After the first look you’ll never need it again — safe to remove.
app.maps.name: Maps
app.maps.desc: Windows Maps. If you use Google Maps or your phone, you can drop this.
app.zunevideo.name: Films & TV
app.zunevideo.desc: Microsoft’s Films & TV player / store front. Fine to remove if you already use VLC or similar.
app.zunemusic.name: Media Player (Groove)
app.zunemusic.desc: The old Groove / music app. Unnecessary if you use Spotify or another player.
app.clipchamp.name: Clipchamp
app.clipchamp.desc: Simple video editor bundled with Windows 11. Remove it if you don’t edit video and want the space back.
app.teams.name: Microsoft Teams
app.teams.desc: Work/school meeting app that sometimes ships with Windows. Remove it if you don’t use it — leave it if work depends on it.
app.store.name: Microsoft Store
app.store.desc: The Microsoft Store — Xbox, many apps, and updates come through here. Removing it puts the system in a bad spot, so the checkbox is locked.
app.photos.name: Photos
app.photos.desc: Default photo and video viewer. Optional if you already use another viewer.
app.calculator.name: Calculator
app.calculator.desc: The Calculator app. Marked critical in the catalog so you can’t delete it by accident here.
app.yourphone.name: Phone Link
app.yourphone.desc: Phone Link between your phone and PC. Safe to remove if you don’t use it; reinstall from the Store anytime.
app.cortana.name: Cortana
app.cortana.desc: Voice assistant app — limited on modern Windows. Safe to remove.
app.widgets.name: Widgets (Web Experience)
app.widgets.desc: Powers the taskbar Widgets panel. Removing it also removes the Widgets icon — some Win11 setups change taskbar behavior afterward.
app.paint3d.name: Paint 3D
app.paint3d.desc: 3D drawing app. Most people stick with classic Paint — safe to remove.
app.print3d.name: Print 3D
app.print3d.desc: 3D printing app. Useless without a 3D printer — safe to remove.
app.todo.name: Microsoft To Do
app.todo.desc: Microsoft To Do task list. Safe to remove if you use something else.
app.quickassist.name: Quick Assist
app.quickassist.desc: Remote support app. Handy in rare support cases — remove only if you’re sure you won’t need it.
tweak.gamemode.name: Enable Game Mode
tweak.gamemode.desc: Tells Windows you’re gaming so background updates and indexing step back and the game gets more focus. Harmless and recommended for gamers.
tweak.gamebar.name: Disable Game Bar Capture
tweak.gamebar.desc: Turns off Game Bar’s always-ready background capture. Instant Win+Alt+G clips may stop working, but FPS usually improves — a favorite for competitive play.
tweak.gamedvr.name: Disable Game DVR Policy
tweak.gamedvr.desc: Policy switch that disables Game DVR / background recording more aggressively. Turn it on if you don’t capture clips.
tweak.hags.name: Hardware-accelerated GPU Scheduling
tweak.hags.desc: Lets the GPU schedule frames with less CPU involvement (HAGS). Can lower latency or cause stutter on some driver/game combos — reboot after changing, and turn it off if things get worse.
tweak.ultimateperf.name: Ultimate Performance Power Plan
tweak.ultimateperf.desc: Unlocks Windows’s hidden Ultimate Performance power plan so CPU/GPU save less power. FPS gets more consistent; laptops drain faster and the PC may run hotter.
tweak.nagle.name: Disable Nagle (TcpAckFrequency)
tweak.nagle.desc: Stops the network from bundling small packets before sending (TcpAckFrequency). Competitive online games may feel a bit snappier; rare networks might lose a little throughput.
tweak.tcpnodelay.name: TCP NoDelay
tweak.tcpnodelay.desc: Same family as disabling Nagle — tells TCP to send immediately instead of waiting. Use it together with the Nagle tweak.
tweak.fso.name: Disable Fullscreen Optimizations Mode
tweak.fso.desc: Pushes games toward classic exclusive fullscreen instead of borderless-window behavior. Helps alt-tab and input in some older or picky titles — not required for every game.
tweak.mmcss.name: MMCSS GPU Priority High
tweak.mmcss.desc: Raises GPU priority in Windows’s Games task profile so the graphics card gets more room while you play. Fine on most PCs (caution-level).
tweak.mmcssprio.name: MMCSS Priority High
tweak.mmcssprio.desc: Raises the scheduling priority number for games so Windows treats them as more important work.
tweak.mmcsssched.name: MMCSS Scheduling Category High
tweak.mmcsssched.desc: Sets the games scheduling category to High. Works as a package with the other MMCSS tweaks.
tweak.bgapps.name: Restrict Background Apps
tweak.bgapps.desc: Limits Store (UWP) apps from quietly running in the background. Less mystery CPU/RAM use; some notifications and sync may lag.
tweak.mouseaccel.name: Disable Enhance Pointer Precision
tweak.mouseaccel.desc: Turns off Enhance pointer precision (mouse acceleration) so aim distance matches hand movement. Desktop mouse feel changes at first — strongly recommended for FPS.
tweak.vbs.name: Disable VBS / Memory Integrity
tweak.vbs.desc: Turns off Memory Integrity / core isolation (HVCI). Some PCs gain more consistent input or FPS, but kernel security gets weaker. Needs a reboot.
tweak.dynamictick.name: Disable Dynamic Tick
tweak.dynamictick.desc: Sets disabledynamictick via bcdedit. May smooth DPC / frame times on some systems — not a miracle everywhere. Needs Administrator; reversible with bcdedit.
tweak.hpet.name: Disable HPET (useplatformclock)
tweak.hpet.desc: Removes forced platform clock usage (bcdedit /deletevalue useplatformclock). Helps latency on some boards, hurts others — measure before keeping it. Needs Administrator.
tweak.telemetry.name: Minimize Telemetry
tweak.telemetry.desc: Sets Windows diagnostic data sent to Microsoft as low as possible. Less “Windows is watching” traffic; Home edition may not reach absolute zero but still cuts a lot.
tweak.adid.name: Disable Advertising ID
tweak.adid.desc: Turns off the advertising ID apps use to track you. Less personalized ads; games keep working.
tweak.tailored.name: Disable Tailored Experiences
tweak.tailored.desc: Stops tips, suggestions, and ads based on your diagnostic data — fewer “just for you” pop-ups.
tweak.cortana.name: Disable Cortana Policy
tweak.cortana.desc: Disables Cortana via policy (already weak on newer Windows). Less voice-assistant background activity.
tweak.bing.name: Disable Bing Search in Start
tweak.bing.desc: Stops Start search from pulling Bing / web results so you only see what’s on your PC — faster and cleaner. A very popular tweak.
tweak.location.name: Deny Location Access
tweak.location.desc: Generally denies apps asking for your location. Better privacy; maps and weather may lose location features.
tweak.activity.name: Disable Activity History
tweak.activity.desc: Stops sending “which app you opened when” history to the cloud / Timeline. Cross-device resume gets weaker.
tweak.visualperf.name: Best Performance Visual Effects
tweak.visualperf.desc: Tells Windows to prefer speed over polish — fewer shadows, smooth scrolls, and animations. The desktop looks flatter but feels lighter.
tweak.animations.name: Disable Window Animations
tweak.animations.desc: Turns off minimize / maximize window animations so windows appear instantly.
tweak.transparency.name: Disable Transparency
tweak.transparency.desc: Turns off frosted-glass transparency on the taskbar and Start. Slightly more matte look, a bit less GPU/CPU on eye candy.
tweak.qos.name: Remove QoS Bandwidth Reserve
tweak.qos.desc: Clears Windows’s default bandwidth reserve (often ~20%). In theory the full pipe is yours — harmless to try even if the gain is small.
tweak.tcpauto.name: TCP Autotuning Normal
tweak.tcpauto.desc: Sets TCP window autotuning to normal via netsh. Useful when downloads or the network behave oddly — a one-shot command.
tweak.dnsflush.name: Flush DNS Cache
tweak.dnsflush.desc: Clears the PC’s cached DNS answers. Handy when a site won’t load, goes to the wrong place, or acts weird after a VPN — harmless one-time cleanup.
tweak.netbios.name: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP
tweak.netbios.desc: Disables NetBIOS on every NetBT interface. Less legacy broadcast chatter on modern networks; very old LAN sharing may be affected.
tweak.deliveryopt.name: Disable Delivery Optimization P2P
tweak.deliveryopt.desc: Stops Windows Update from sharing updates P2P with other PCs. Updates still come from Microsoft; your upload isn’t wasted — great on a data cap.
tweak.wupause.name: Disable Windows Update Service
tweak.wupause.desc: Fully stops the Windows Update service. No surprise updates, but also no security patches — OK for a short pause before a tournament or stream, then turn it back on. Needs “allow dangerous actions”.
tweak.taskceip.name: Disable CEIP Consolidator Task
tweak.taskceip.desc: Disables the Customer Experience Improvement scheduled task that sends usage summaries to Microsoft. One less telemetry job.
tweak.taskusbceip.name: Disable USB CEIP Task
tweak.taskusbceip.desc: Disables the CEIP task that tracks USB device usage. Less telemetry; USB devices still work.
tweak.classicmenu.name: Classic Context Menu
tweak.classicmenu.desc: Restores the full classic right-click menu on Windows 11 instead of the compact one. Explorer restarts briefly when you toggle it.
tweak.copilot.name: Disable Windows Copilot
tweak.copilot.desc: Turns off Windows Copilot via policy (taskbar / Win+C). Windows 11 only.
tweak.recall.name: Disable Windows Recall
tweak.recall.desc: Disables Windows Recall / AI screen-data analysis via policy. Recommended for privacy on Windows 11.
tweak.startiris.name: Hide Start Recommendations
tweak.startiris.desc: Turns off Start menu “recommended / Iris” content for a cleaner Start. Explorer may restart.
tweak.widgets.name: Disable Widgets / News Feed
tweak.widgets.desc: Disables taskbar Widgets and the News and interests feed. Less background chatter; Explorer may restart.
tweak.inking.name: Disable Inking & Typing Personalization
tweak.inking.desc: Stops sending keyboard / handwriting usage data to Microsoft for personalization. Suggestions get more generic; privacy improves.
tweak.feedbackfreq.name: Silence Feedback Frequency
tweak.feedbackfreq.desc: Stops Windows “Give us feedback” survey pop-ups.
tweak.onlinespeech.name: Disable Online Speech Recognition
tweak.onlinespeech.desc: Stops sending voice data to the cloud for speech recognition. Online speech features turn off; local ones stay.
tweak.powerthrottle.name: Disable Power Throttling
tweak.powerthrottle.desc: Stops Windows from throttling CPU for background / inactive windows. Minimized helpers like Discord get throttled less while gaming; laptop battery may suffer.
tweak.sysresp.name: Multimedia System Responsiveness
tweak.sysresp.desc: Sets the CPU reserve for background tasks (default ~20%) to zero so games and multimedia get more CPU time.
tweak.coreparking.name: Disable CPU Core Parking
tweak.coreparking.desc: Keeps all CPU cores awake on the current power plan (no core parking). Fewer lags on sudden load spikes; higher power use.
tweak.darkmode.name: Enable Dark Mode
tweak.darkmode.desc: Turns on dark theme for apps and the system UI.
tweak.lockscreenads.name: Disable Lock Screen Ads / Tips
tweak.lockscreenads.desc: Turns off Windows Spotlight ads and tip overlays on the lock screen so you get a plain static image.
tweak.showext.name: Show File Extensions & Hidden Files
tweak.showext.desc: Shows file extensions and hidden files in Explorer — easier to spot fake “photo.jpg.exe” files. Explorer restarts.
tweak.taskbarleft.name: Align Taskbar Left
tweak.taskbarleft.desc: Moves Windows 11 taskbar icons back to the classic left alignment. Explorer restarts.
tweak.hidechat.name: Hide Taskbar Chat Icon
tweak.hidechat.desc: Hides the Teams / Chat icon on the taskbar. Explorer restarts.
tweak.searchicon.name: Shrink Search Box to Icon
tweak.searchicon.desc: Shrinks the wide taskbar search box to a small icon. Explorer restarts.
tweak.hidetaskview.name: Hide Task View Button
tweak.hidetaskview.desc: Hides the Task View button on the taskbar without uninstalling anything. Explorer restarts.
tweak.explorerthispc.name: Open Explorer to This PC
tweak.explorerthispc.desc: Makes File Explorer open to This PC instead of Home.
tweak.netthrottle.name: Reset Network Throttling Index
tweak.netthrottle.desc: Removes Windows’s multimedia/game network packet processing limit. Under heavy online traffic, packet delay may drop.
tweak.ipv6.name: Disable IPv6
tweak.ipv6.desc: Disables IPv6 system-wide. Some modern services (console crossplay, certain VPNs) may need IPv6 — don’t combine with Prefer IPv4. Use only if IPv6 is causing connectivity issues; reboot recommended.
tweak.nicpower.name: Disable NIC Power Saving
tweak.nicpower.desc: Stops Windows from sleeping network adapters to save power. Can reduce random micro-disconnects and lag spikes in online games.

preset.gamer.name: Gamer Mode
preset.gamer.desc: One click for Game Mode, Game Bar/DVR off, a strong power plan, MMCSS, lighter visuals, less telemetry, SysMain off, and similar gaming tweaks. Read the preview list, then apply on a gaming PC.
preset.balanced.name: Balanced Mode
preset.balanced.desc: Light touch: Game Mode plus basic privacy, without aggressive service shutdowns. For when you want a bit of polish without risking Windows.
preset.minimal.name: Minimal / Server Mode
preset.minimal.desc: As lean as possible — telemetry, animations, background apps, unneeded services. Better for a second PC or HTPC; try Gamer first on your main gaming machine.
preset.laptop.name: Laptop / Battery Mode
preset.laptop.desc: Skips aggressive gaming power tweaks and focuses on telemetry cuts, lighter visuals, and fewer background apps — balanced for battery life.
preset.privacymax.name: Maximum Privacy
preset.privacymax.desc: More privacy than Balanced without going full Minimal: telemetry, location, advertising ID, and personalization tweaks in one profile.
preset.defaults.name: Restore Defaults (Undo Session)
preset.defaults.desc: Reverts reversible changes from this WinCleaner session (Undo All). Removed apps don’t come back — reinstall those from the Store.

app.copilot.name: Copilot
app.copilot.desc: Windows Copilot chat on the taskbar / Start. Remove carefully if you actually use it; you can reinstall from the Store.
app.bingsearch.name: Bing Search
app.bingsearch.desc: Bing extras that inject web results into Windows Search. Local search still works without it.
app.outlook.name: Outlook (new)
app.outlook.desc: The new Outlook for Windows app. Safe to remove if you use classic Outlook or another mail client — keep it if this is your daily mail.
app.stickynotes.name: Sticky Notes
app.stickynotes.desc: Sticky Notes. Safe to remove if you don’t use it; notes can come back via Store / Microsoft account.
app.powerautomate.name: Power Automate
app.powerautomate.desc: Desktop automation / flows app. Safe to remove if you never built a flow.
app.devhome.name: Dev Home
app.devhome.desc: Microsoft’s developer dashboard. Safe to remove if you’re not using it (Windows 11).
app.xboxtcui.name: Xbox TCUI
app.xboxtcui.desc: Xbox title-callable UI used by Game Bar / Game Pass popups. Leave it if you keep Game Bar or Game Pass.
app.xboxspeech.name: Xbox speech overlay
app.xboxspeech.desc: Xbox Game Bar speech-to-text overlay. Safe to remove if you don’t use in-game voice captions.
app.family.name: Microsoft Family
app.family.desc: Family Safety / parental controls companion. Safe to remove if you don’t manage child accounts on this PC.
app.startexperiences.name: Start experiences
app.startexperiences.desc: Start menu recommendations and suggested-app experiences on Windows 11. Start still works without it; suggestions just change.
search.title: Search results
search.subtitle: Matches across all categories
tweak.hibernation.name: Disable Hibernation
tweak.hibernation.desc: Turns off hibernation and deletes the large hiberfil.sys file. Frees disk space; you lose hibernate / hybrid sleep.
tweak.wpbt.name: Disable WPBT Execution
tweak.wpbt.desc: Blocks OEM WPBT payloads from running at boot so some vendor bloat can’t reinstall itself. Rare OEM tools may depend on it.
tweak.endtask.name: End Task From Taskbar
tweak.endtask.desc: Adds End task to the Windows 11 taskbar app right-click menu.
tweak.devmeta.name: Block Device Metadata From Network
tweak.devmeta.desc: Stops Windows from downloading device companion metadata from the internet — less background network chatter.
tweak.storesearch.name: Disable Store Search Suggestions
tweak.storesearch.desc: Blocks access to the Microsoft Store local search database (WinUtil-style). Fragile — Store updates may reset it and Store search can break.
tweak.folderdiscovery.name: Disable Explorer Folder Type Discovery
tweak.folderdiscovery.desc: Stops Explorer from auto-guessing folder templates (clears Bags/BagMRU). Needs sign-out or reboot; undo only partly clears bags again.
tweak.homegallery.name: Unpin Explorer Home and Gallery
tweak.homegallery.desc: Unpins Home and Gallery from the Explorer navigation pane on Windows 11. Use “Open Explorer to This PC” separately if you want that too. Explorer restarts.
tweak.reservedstorage.name: Disable Reserved Storage
tweak.reservedstorage.desc: Disables Windows Reserved Storage via DISM and can reclaim several GB. Updates may need more free space afterward.
tweak.storagesense.name: Disable Storage Sense
tweak.storagesense.desc: Turns off Storage Sense automatic cleanup.
tweak.ipv4pref.name: Prefer IPv4 Over IPv6
tweak.ipv4pref.desc: Makes Windows prefer IPv4 without fully disabling IPv6. Don’t combine with Disable IPv6 — pick one. Reboot recommended.
tweak.teredo.name: Disable Teredo
tweak.teredo.desc: Disables the Teredo IPv6 tunneling interface via netsh.
tweak.utctime.name: Hardware Clock Uses UTC
tweak.utctime.desc: Treats the hardware clock as UTC (helpful for dual-boot with Linux). On Windows-only PCs the clock can skew until corrected. Reboot required.
tweak.svchostsplit.name: Disable svchost Service Splitting
tweak.svchostsplit.desc: Groups services into fewer svchost processes. Dangerous — instability can take down more services at once. Reboot required.
tweak.traynotif.name: Disable Notification Center and Toasts
tweak.traynotif.desc: Disables Notification Center and toast notifications. You’ll miss system and app alerts.
tweak.longpaths.name: Enable Win32 Long Paths
tweak.longpaths.desc: Allows paths longer than 260 characters for compatible apps.
tweak.verboselogon.name: Verbose Logon Messages
tweak.verboselogon.desc: Shows detailed status text while signing in or out.
tweak.bsodverbose.name: Verbose Blue Screen Details
tweak.bsodverbose.desc: Shows technical BSOD details and disables the sad-face emoticon.
tweak.numlock.name: Num Lock On at Startup
tweak.numlock.desc: Turns Num Lock on for the logon screen and the current user.
tweak.scrollbars.name: Always Show Scrollbars
tweak.scrollbars.desc: Keeps scrollbars always visible instead of auto-hiding.
tweak.stickykeys.name: Disable Sticky Keys Shortcut
tweak.stickykeys.desc: Disables Sticky Keys so the Shift-key popup doesn’t interrupt games.
tweak.settingshome.name: Hide Settings Home Page
tweak.settingshome.desc: Hides the Windows 11 Settings home / recommendation page.
tweak.lockscreen.name: Disable Lock Screen
tweak.lockscreen.desc: Skips the lock screen and goes straight to the password/PIN prompt. Slightly weaker if someone has physical access to the PC.
tweak.s0standby.name: Keep Network On in Connected Standby
tweak.s0standby.desc: Allows network connectivity during Modern Standby (S0) while on AC power.
tweak.s3sleep.name: Prefer Classic S3 Sleep
tweak.s3sleep.desc: Prefers classic S3 sleep on supported hardware. Not all modern laptops support it; reboot required.
tweak.batterypercent.name: Show Battery Percentage
tweak.batterypercent.desc: Shows the numeric battery percentage in the system tray.
tweak.loginblur.name: Disable Logon Acrylic Blur
tweak.loginblur.desc: Disables the acrylic blur behind the sign-in screen.
tweak.windowsnap.name: Disable Window Snapping
tweak.windowsnap.desc: Turns off Aero Snap / window arrangement. Useful if snapping fights your games or multi-monitor layout.
tweak.mpo.name: Disable Multiplane Overlay (MPO)
tweak.mpo.desc: Disables DWM multiplane overlays. Try this for black screens, stutter, or overlay bugs with some GPUs/fullscreen games. Reboot required.

app.crossdevice.name: Mobile Devices (Cross Device)
app.crossdevice.desc: Cross-device experience package between your Microsoft devices. Safe to remove if you don’t use those features.
app.soundrecorder.name: Sound Recorder
app.soundrecorder.desc: Simple voice recorder. Safe to remove if you don’t need it.
app.clock.name: Clock
app.clock.desc: Clock, alarms, and timers app. Optional if you don’t use it.
app.paint.name: Paint
app.paint.desc: Classic Paint. Leave it unless you have a replacement — many people still open it for quick edits.
app.notepad.name: Notepad
app.notepad.desc: Notepad. Locked as a basic system text editor so you don’t remove it by mistake.
app.snip.name: Snipping Tool
app.snip.desc: Snipping Tool / screenshot app. Keep it unless you already use ShareX or similar.
app.camera.name: Camera
app.camera.desc: Camera app. Safe to remove on a desktop without a webcam.
tweak.feathyperv.name: Enable Hyper-V
tweak.feathyperv.desc: Turns the Hyper-V Windows feature on or off. Needed for some VMs and sandboxes; uses resources when enabled.
tweak.featwsl.name: Enable WSL + Virtual Machine Platform
tweak.featwsl.desc: Turns Windows Subsystem for Linux on or off.
tweak.featsandbox.name: Enable Windows Sandbox
tweak.featsandbox.desc: Turns Windows Sandbox on or off. Needs virtualization support.
tweak.featdotnet.name: Enable .NET Framework 2/3/4 Features
tweak.featdotnet.desc: Toggles older .NET Framework features some desktop apps still need.
tweak.featmedia.name: Enable Legacy Media Components
tweak.featmedia.desc: Toggles legacy Windows media features (older codecs / Media Features).
tweak.featnfs.name: Enable NFS Client
tweak.featnfs.desc: Toggles the NFS client feature for mounting NFS network shares.
tweak.featf8.name: Enable Legacy F8 Boot Menu
tweak.featf8.desc: Restores the legacy F8 advanced boot menu behavior where supported.
tweak.wurecommended.name: Recommended Windows Update Deferrals
tweak.wurecommended.desc: Limits or controls optional / recommended Windows Update offerings so fewer extras install themselves.
tools.ntp.desc: Syncs the clock with an NTP time server so Windows time stays accurate.

tools.autologon.desc: Signs in automatically with the selected account (stores credentials). Convenient on a home PC — weaker if others can touch the machine.
tools.wingetRepair.desc: Repairs or re-registers winget / App Installer so package installs work again.
